preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100) representing the number of operators.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 3 or len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each subsequent line is either a 'typedef A B' or 'typeof A' operator, where A and B (if present) are valid type expressions.

preconditions.expression: all('typedef' in line or 'typeof' in line for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Every operator line starts with either 'typedef' or 'typeof'.

preconditions.expression: all('*' not in name and '&' not in name and name not in ['void', 'errtype'] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for name in line.split() if name not in ['typedef', 'typeof'] and name.islower() and len(name) <= 20)
preconditions.description: Type names (B in typedef) are non-empty lowercase Latin letters (1-20 chars) and do not contain '*' or '&'.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()[1]) <= 100 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if 'typedef' in line)
preconditions.description: The type expression A in 'typedef A B' has no more than 100 characters (including '*' and '&').

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line in ['void', 'errtype'] or (stdout_line.startswith('void') and all(c in '*' for c in stdout_line[4:])) or stdout_line == 'errtype' for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines() if stdout_line)
postconditions.description: For every 'typeof A' operator, the output is either 'void' followed by zero or more '*' (e.g., 'void*', 'void**'), or 'errtype'.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.splitlines()) == sum(1 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if 'typeof' in line))
postconditions.description: The number of output lines equals the number of 'typeof' operators in the input.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout.splitlines()[i] == resolve_type(stdin.splitlines()[1:][j]) for i, j in enumerate([k for k, line in enumerate(stdin.splitlines()[1:]) if 'typeof' in line]))
postconditions.description: Each output line corresponds to the resolved type of the 'typeof A' operator at the same position in the input, where resolve_type() is a function that computes the type according to the &K* rules.
